paper_title: Do direct detection experiments constrain axionlike particles coupled to electrons?
notes: This is a theory/reinterpretation paper arguing that keV-MeV ALP dark matter coupled to electrons decays too fast (a->gamma gamma) to be dark matter, invalidating direct-detection limits (GERDA, EDELWEISS-III, SuperCDMS, Majorana) and noting X-ray/gamma-ray astronomy supersedes them for 6 keV-1 MeV. It does not present its own new tabulated exclusion limit; the relevant curves (lifetime boundary and X-ray/gamma-ray exclusion) are shown only in Fig. 2 without extractable numerical data. No new measured limit dataset is provided. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Traced the lowermost exclusion boundary (light grey X-ray/gamma-ray limits on lifetime), which supersedes lab limits for m_a > 6 keV. Below ~5 keV, direct detection limits (LUX/XENON1T) plateau near 1e-13, which form the boundary at low mass. The light grey astrophysical constraint dominates the lower boundary above ~6 keV, dropping steeply with mass roughly as inferred from lifetime scaling. Values read on log-log scale; the boundary has significant jaggedness in the actual figure. | Calibration: No calibration needed
